_readme: Feature registry (TWI-8). Source of truth for the catalog and What's New.
This is NOT a Django loaddata serialization -- rows are matched by 'key' and upserted,
so re-running after every release updates copy without duplicating rows or losing
UserAcknowledgement history. Removing an entry from this file
deactivates it; nothing is ever deleted.
Display order comes from list position, so there is no 'order' field to keep in sync.
Role guides (TWI-12) live in the top-level 'role_guides' list and are matched on 'role',
which must be a value from core.models.ALL_ROLES so it lines up with tasks.Task.owner.

areas.name: Getting in
areas.description: Signing in, and what to do when you cannot. This is the only part of the guide visible before you sign in.

features.name: Sign in
features.short_description: Sign in with the email address the fraternity has on file for you.
features.long_description: Accounts are created for you when you are pledged or initiated. There is no sign-up page. If your email address has changed, use 'Update my info without signing in' below.

features.name: Find my username or badge number
features.short_description: Look yourself up by name and chapter to find the username and badge number on file.
features.long_description: The lookup sits on the sign-in page. Give your university and badge number and a reset link is emailed to the address on file, with the address partly masked so you can check it is the one you still use.

features.name: Reset my password
features.short_description: Send yourself a password reset link.
features.long_description: The link goes to the email address on file. If you no longer have access to that address, update your info first and then reset.

features.name: Update my info without signing in
features.short_description: Change the email address, phone number or address we hold for you, without an account.
features.long_description: Look yourself up, confirm your identity, and submit the changes. A National Officer reviews the request before it takes effect.

areas.name: Getting started
areas.description: Your home page, your own record, and the policies you agree to.

features.name: Home dashboard
features.short_description: Announcements, the tasks your chapter still owes, and your region's numbers, on one page.

features.name: My profile
features.short_description: Your badge number, status, roles, service hours and award history.

features.name: Edit my info
features.short_description: Update your email, phone, address, graduation year and major.
features.long_description: Keeping your graduation date right matters: it drives when you are moved to alumnus status and whether you keep receiving chapter mail.

features.name: My profile picture
features.short_description: Upload the photo that appears next to your name in the roster and directories.

features.name: Email preferences
features.short_description: Choose which optional fraternity mailings you receive.
features.long_description: Under 'Email Preferences / Unsubscribe' on your own info page. Every fraternity email also carries an unsubscribe link that switches off just that category. Compliance mail, such as risk management reminders, cannot be turned off. Some mailings are sent from systems that sync monthly, so a change can take a few weeks to reach them.

features.name: Terms of service
features.short_description: The end user licence agreement you accept when you sign in.

features.name: Electronic business terms
features.short_description: How the fraternity treats electronic signatures and electronically submitted forms.

features.name: Privacy notice
features.short_description: What the fraternity stores about you and who can see it.

features.name: About
features.short_description: What the Chapter Management Tool is, who maintains it, and how to report a problem.

areas.name: My chapter
areas.description: Your chapter's own page: what it has submitted, how it is scoring, and who is watching.

features.name: Chapter home
features.short_description: Your chapter's officers, advisors, school and status in one place.

features.name: Chapter activity
features.short_description: A running log of everything your chapter has submitted and when.

features.name: Chapter audit history
features.short_description: Past audit submissions for your chapter.

features.name: Chapter directory
features.short_description: Every chapter in the fraternity, with school, region and status.

features.name: Chapter scores
features.short_description: How your chapter is scoring this year, broken down by what earns points.
features.long_description: Scores come from what your chapter submits: events, service, forms and reports. Open a score line to see exactly which submissions counted.

features.name: Chapter notes
features.short_description: Record a note against a chapter that other National Officers will see.

features.name: Member notes
features.short_description: Record a note against an individual member's record.

areas.name: Roster & members
areas.description: Who is in your chapter, and the academic and service data the fraternity keeps for them.

features.name: Chapter roster
features.short_description: Every active, pledge and alumnus member of your chapter, with status and contact details.

features.name: Enter member GPAs
features.short_description: Record each member's GPA for the term.
features.long_description: GPAs feed the scholarship score and the academic reports the national office runs. Enter them once per term.

features.name: Enter service hours
features.short_description: Record service hours for members of your chapter.

features.name: External organizations
features.short_description: Other student organizations your chapter's members belong to.

features.name: Log external org participation
features.short_description: Add an organization a member takes part in outside Theta Tau.

features.name: Member search (all chapters)
features.short_description: Find any member in the fraternity, across every chapter.

areas.name: Events & attendance
areas.description: Running chapter events and recording who came.

features.name: Chapter events
features.short_description: Every event your chapter has scheduled or held, with its type and score value.

features.name: Add an event
features.short_description: Schedule an event, choose its type, and set how it scores.
features.long_description: Event type decides which score it feeds, so pick it carefully. You can copy last year's event rather than retyping it.

features.name: Events calendar
features.short_description: Your chapter's events in a month view.

features.name: Calendar subscriptions
features.short_description: Feed chapter events straight into Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar.

features.name: Subscribe to a chapter's calendar
features.short_description: Get a subscription link for any chapter's events.
features.long_description: Open a chapter and use Subscribe to these events under Public Events. You can add the chapter to a feed you already have instead of starting a new one, so several chapters can share a single calendar.

features.name: Add my tasks to my calendar
features.short_description: Put your chapter's task due dates in your own calendar.
features.long_description: Create a to-dos-only feed from Chapter To-do Reminders. Leave the officer list empty for every task, or pick the offices you hold so your calendar only carries what you owe.

features.name: All events (all chapters)
features.short_description: Every event across the fraternity, filterable by region and type.

features.name: Pending event reviews
features.short_description: Events waiting on a National Officer to approve or reject them.

features.name: Take attendance
features.short_description: Mark who attended an event, in bulk, from the event's own page.
features.long_description: Open the event from Chapter events and use the attendance roster. Attendance is per-event, so there is no single page to link to here.

features.name: RSVP for an event
features.short_description: Say whether you are coming, from the event's page.
features.long_description: Open the event from Chapter events or the calendar. RSVPs are per-event, so there is no single page to link to here.

features.name: Log my own attendance
features.short_description: Record that you attended an event that was missed when the roster was taken.
features.long_description: Use Log missing attendance at the foot of the attendance card on your profile. You cannot create events here. Search for the national or chapter event you attended.

features.name: Upload national attendance
features.short_description: Bulk-load attendance for a national event from a spreadsheet.

features.name: National attendance match queue
features.short_description: Resolve uploaded attendance rows that did not match a member automatically.

areas.name: Tasks & goals
areas.description: What your chapter owes the national office, what it has set out to do, and what it has sent in.

features.name: Chapter tasks
features.short_description: Every obligation your chapter has, who owns it, and when it is due.
features.long_description: Tasks are assigned to an officer role, not a person, so they follow the office through elections. Missing a task costs your chapter score.

features.name: My workflow tasks
features.short_description: Forms waiting on you to review, approve or complete.
features.long_description: Multi-step forms such as initiation, discipline, premature alumnus and award nominations move between people. Anything waiting on your chapter shows under 'Chapter Process Reminders' at the top of the task list, and only the member it is assigned to gets a link to act on it.

features.name: Chapter goals
features.short_description: The goals your chapter set for the year and how they are tracking.
features.long_description: This page shows the goals of whichever chapter you are currently viewing as. Regional Directors and National Officers pick a chapter with the switcher in the bar across the top of the page, then open this to see what that chapter set out to do.

features.name: Set a goal
features.short_description: Record a goal for your chapter with a target and a date.
features.long_description: The goal is recorded against whichever chapter you are currently viewing as, so a Regional Director or National Officer switches to the chapter first using the bar across the top of the page. Goals are usually agreed during a visit and written down here so the next visit has something to measure against.

features.name: Submissions
features.short_description: Everything your chapter has submitted for score, with dates and score types.

features.name: Add a submission
features.short_description: Send in something your chapter did that earns score, then pick the score type and attach the evidence.

areas.name: Forms & workflows
areas.description: Every form the fraternity asks for, from pledging a new member to reporting an officer election.

features.name: Initiation report
features.short_description: Report the members your chapter has initiated and order their badges.
features.long_description: Select the pledges being initiated, confirm their details, and submit. Badge numbers are assigned by the national office once the report is processed.

features.name: Pledge / new member form

features.long_description: This is the only form a prospective member fills in themselves, so it works without an account. Pledges must be reported before they can be initiated.

features.name: Graduate members
features.short_description: Report members who are graduating. Select several at once and fill one row each.

features.name: Report a co-op or study abroad
features.short_description: Report a member leaving temporarily for a co-op, internship, or study abroad.

features.name: Report a military deployment

features.name: Report a withdrawal from school
features.short_description: Report a member withdrawing from school.

features.name: Report a transfer to another school
features.short_description: Report a member transferring to another school.

features.name: Premature alumnus request
features.short_description: Ask for a member to be moved to alumnus status before they graduate.
features.long_description: Reviewed by the national office. Use this rather than a withdrawal when the member is staying in school but stepping back from the chapter.

features.name: Return student request
features.short_description: Bring a member back to active status after a leave, co-op or deployment.

features.name: Resignation
features.short_description: Resign your membership of the fraternity.
features.long_description: A resignation is reviewed by your chapter and then by the national office. It is not reversible once accepted.

features.name: Resignations
features.short_description: Resignation requests submitted by your chapter's members.

features.name: Alumni exclusion request

features.name: All alumni exclusions

features.long_description: Until this is submitted, the outgoing officers keep the access and keep getting the reminder emails. Submit it the week the election happens.

features.name: National officers directory

features.name: Chapter bylaws

features.name: All chapter bylaws

The next step lists everyone you marked, with a page to print for each and a download-all option. role_guides.title: Regent
role_guides.summary: You are accountable for the chapter as a whole: its officers, its compliance with national policy, and its standing. Almost everything national headquarters needs from your chapter arrives as a task on your home page, and several of those tasks carry your name. Start there, then work down this page.

steps.title: Start with your task list
steps.body: Your home page lists every task the chapter still owes, with its due date. Tasks assigned to the Regent are yours to complete or delegate, but the chapter is graded on all of them, not just yours.

steps.title: Sign the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own RMP each term, you included. It is not something the chapter files once. The site keeps prompting you until you do, and members who have not signed count against the chapter.

steps.title: Run the health and safety education programs
steps.body: Once a year the chapter must run an alcohol and drug awareness program, an anti-harassment program, and a mental health recognition program, then report all three here.

steps.title: Complete the annual audit
steps.body: The audit is signed by the Regent, Vice Regent, Scribe, Treasurer and Corresponding Secretary. Fill it in with your Treasurer, who holds the numbers.

steps.title: Nominate your Outstanding Student Member
steps.body: One member each year. Nominations close well before Convention, so put it on the chapter calendar early.

steps.title: Put your members up for awards
steps.body: Member, chapter and region awards all run through the same nomination flow. Nobody outside the chapter will do this for you.

steps.title: Set goals for the term
steps.body: Goals are how the chapter tells its Regional Director what it is trying to achieve, and how that progress gets recognised at the end of the term.

steps.title: Watch your chapter score
steps.body: The score rolls up submissions, events, service hours and attendance. Check it mid-term rather than at the end, while there is still time to close a gap.

role_guides.title: Vice Regent
role_guides.summary: You own the candidate program end to end: reporting who was pledged, running their education, and reporting their initiation. Each of those has a deadline, and the fees the chapter is invoiced follow directly from what you submit, so a late form is also a billing problem.

steps.title: Submit the pledge form as soon as you pledge a class
steps.body: The pledge form is what creates candidate records. Until it is filed the candidates do not exist on the roster and cannot be initiated.

steps.title: Order pledge pins
steps.body: Pins are ordered separately from the pledge form and ship from a vendor, so order early.

steps.title: File your new member education program
steps.body: The program you intend to run, submitted once a year for review.

steps.title: Track candidates on the roster
steps.body: The roster shows every candidate and their current status. Use it to check nobody has been missed before initiation.

steps.title: Report the initiation
steps.body: Filed immediately after the ceremony. This is what turns candidates into members and triggers the initiation invoice.

steps.title: Sign the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own RMP each term, you included.

steps.title: Sign the annual audit
steps.body: The Treasurer fills it in; you are one of the officers who signs it.

role_guides.title: Scribe
role_guides.summary: You keep the record. The roster is the fraternity's single source of truth for who is a member, where they are and how to reach them, and nearly every other report is built from it. Keeping it current is the whole job, and it is continuous rather than once a term.

steps.title: Keep the roster current
steps.body: Add, correct and update members as things change. Invoices, award eligibility and mailing lists all read from the roster, so an error here shows up everywhere else.

steps.title: Report officer elections
steps.body: File within a week of the election. Officer records control who can sign what in this system, so a late report locks your new officers out of their own forms.

steps.title: File status changes when members leave
steps.body: Graduating, co-op, military leave, withdrawal and transfer each have their own form. Filing them is what stops the chapter being invoiced for members who are gone.

steps.title: Submit premature alumnus requests
steps.body: For members who need alumnus status before graduating. Requires chapter approval and national review, so start early.

steps.title: Record the roll book
steps.body: The roll book page is the permanent signed record of each initiate. Mark the candidate 'Roll Book' on the initiation selection form to generate theirs.

steps.title: Take attendance at chapter events
steps.body: Attendance feeds the chapter score and the service-hour totals members rely on for their own records.

steps.title: Sign the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own RMP each term, you included.

steps.title: Sign the annual audit
steps.body: The Treasurer fills it in; you are one of the officers who signs it.

role_guides.title: Treasurer
role_guides.summary: You are responsible for the chapter's money and for everything it owes nationally. Invoices are raised automatically from what the other officers submit, so a surprise on the balance is usually a roster change or an initiation report you have not seen yet. Read the invoice page before every chapter meeting.

steps.title: Know what your chapter owes
steps.body: Every national charge appears on the invoice page with what it was for. This is the page to bring to a chapter meeting.

steps.title: Pay dues on time
steps.body: Dues are invoiced per member straight from the roster. Late payment affects the chapter's standing, not just its balance.

steps.title: Pay the insurance premium
steps.body: Billed annually and separately from dues.

steps.title: Lead the annual audit
steps.body: The audit is mostly your numbers. The other officers sign it, but you are the one who fills it in.

steps.title: Review the chapter inventory
steps.body: Badges, jewelry, ritual equipment and other chapter property.

steps.title: Refer unpaid member accounts for collection
steps.body: When a member will not pay, this is the formal route. Do not quietly write the debt off locally, because the chapter stays liable for it.

steps.title: Sign the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own RMP each term, you included.

role_guides.title: Corresponding Secretary
role_guides.summary: You are the chapter's voice to everyone outside it: the national office, your alumni, and The Gear. The Gear article and the alumni newsletter are the only regular contact most alumni have with the chapter, so they matter more than their size suggests.

steps.title: Write the chapter's Gear article
steps.body: The Gear is the fraternity's magazine and every chapter contributes. A short article with a photo is enough.

steps.title: Send the alumni newsletter
steps.body: Once a year, to the alumni on your roster.

steps.title: Keep alumni contact details current
steps.body: Alumni sit on the roster like everyone else. Correct their details as they come back to you, or the newsletter will not reach them next year.

steps.title: Export the chapter's contacts instead of retyping them
steps.body: Contact sync pushes the chapter's contacts into Google or Microsoft, or downloads them as a vCard file.

steps.title: Sign the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own RMP each term, you included.

steps.title: Sign the annual audit
steps.body: The Treasurer fills it in; you are one of the officers who signs it.

role_guides.title: New Member Educator
role_guides.summary: You run candidate education day to day, alongside the Vice Regent who is formally accountable for it. Nothing here is invoiced to you, but the roster, the initiation report and the depledge survey all depend on you telling the Scribe and Vice Regent what has changed.

steps.title: Read the program the chapter filed
steps.body: The new member education program on file with headquarters is what you are delivering. Start by reading the current one.

steps.title: Check the candidate list on the roster
steps.body: Candidates appear on the roster once the Vice Regent files the pledge form. If someone is missing, that form has not been submitted.

steps.title: Log education sessions as events
steps.body: Recording sessions as events is what gets candidate attendance onto the record, which the chapter is scored on.

steps.title: Make sure every candidate is on the pledge form
steps.body: A candidate who was never reported cannot be initiated, and the omission usually surfaces the week of the ceremony.

steps.title: Know the health and safety programs
steps.body: Alcohol and drug awareness, anti-harassment, and mental health recognition. Candidates should attend all three.

steps.title: Expect the depledge survey
steps.body: Any candidate who leaves before initiation is emailed a short survey with their own personal link, so there is no page here to open. Results come back in aggregate, never by name. It is how the fraternity learns why candidates leave.

role_guides.title: Risk Management Chair
role_guides.summary: For permissions you are a member, not a chapter officer, but you own real obligations. The Risk Management Policies, the health and safety education programs and the chapter's event practices all run through you, and the chapter's compliance record depends on them happening on time.

steps.title: Read the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: Every member signs their own each term, you included. You should know them better than anyone.

steps.title: Organise the health and safety education programs
steps.body: Alcohol and drug awareness, anti-harassment, and mental health recognition, at least one of each per year. The Regent files the report; you run the programs.

steps.title: Look ahead at the events calendar
steps.body: The chapter events list is the easiest way to see what is coming and flag anything that needs a plan before it happens rather than after.

steps.title: Know the Bill of Rights
steps.body: What every member and candidate is entitled to. Read it once; refer to it when something goes wrong.

steps.title: Know where the chapter's bylaws are
steps.body: Chapter bylaws are filed here and reviewed nationally. Risk decisions often turn on what they actually say.

role_guides.title: Chapter Adviser
role_guides.summary: You advise; you do not run the chapter. But you are the continuity between officer terms and usually the first person a Regional Director asks. Most of what you need here is read-only: the task list, the score, the roster and the calendar.

steps.title: See what the chapter owes
steps.body: The task list shows every outstanding national obligation with its due date. It is the fastest way to tell whether a chapter is in trouble.

steps.title: Read the chapter's score
steps.body: Scores roll up submissions, events, service hours and attendance, so a falling score usually points at a specific officer who needs help.

steps.title: Know who the officers are
steps.body: Officer records change every year and the chapter does not always tell you. Check after each election.

steps.title: Watch the events calendar
steps.body: What the chapter is actually doing, as opposed to what it reports.

steps.title: Know the Risk Management Policies
steps.body: You will be asked about them, usually at short notice.

steps.title: Keep your own details current
steps.body: Advisers are on the roster too, and the national office contacts you using what is there.

role_guides.title: Regional Director
role_guides.summary: You cover every chapter in your region. The region pages roll up what you would otherwise have to visit each chapter to find: outstanding tasks, scores, officers and advisers. You also hold National Officer access, so the fraternity-wide dashboards, event queues and balance reports are open to you. Start from your own region page and work outward.

steps.title: Start at your region page
steps.body: Your region, its chapters, and how each of them is doing, on one page.

steps.title: Watch the region dashboard
steps.body: The same charts the national dashboard uses, scoped to your region.

steps.title: Compare against the whole fraternity
steps.body: The national dashboard is the same view with no region filter. Use it to tell a region-wide problem apart from a fraternity-wide one before you raise it with a chapter.

steps.title: Check outstanding tasks across the region
steps.body: Every chapter's overdue obligations in one list. This is the page to work from before a check-in call.

steps.title: Follow the scores
steps.body: Every chapter's score, side by side. Filter to your region to see who is drifting, and open a chapter to see which categories are costing it points.

steps.title: Keep an eye on chapter balances
steps.body: What each chapter owes the national office. A balance that keeps growing is usually the first sign of a Treasurer who needs help, well before anything else shows up.

steps.title: Review the events waiting on you
steps.body: Events a chapter has submitted for national review sit in this queue until an officer approves or rejects them. Nothing chases you, so make a habit of opening it.

steps.title: See what your chapters are actually running
steps.body: Every event across the fraternity, filterable by region and type. A chapter running nothing but meetings is worth a conversation.

steps.title: Watch turnout, not just event counts
steps.body: The events and attendance dashboard pairs how much a chapter is running with how many members turn up. The gap between the two is the number that matters.

steps.title: Know who the officers are
steps.body: Officer records change every year. Check after each chapter's election so you are writing to the right people.

steps.title: Know who the advisers are
steps.body: Advisers are your continuity when a chapter's officers turn over.

steps.title: Put your region's contacts on your phone
steps.body: The region officer list has a Sync contacts button. Connect a Google or Microsoft account and the details stay current as chapters hold elections, or take a vCard file instead.

steps.title: Put the national officers on your phone too
steps.body: The national officer directory carries the same Sync contacts button, so you can reach the right national officer without hunting for an address.

steps.title: Leave notes on the chapters you visit
steps.body: A chapter note is how the next Regional Director knows what happened before they arrived, and how the national office sees the history behind a score.

steps.title: Set and review goals with each chapter
steps.body: Goals are scoped to the chapter you are viewing as, so switch to the chapter in the bar across the top of the page first. A visit can then open with what the chapter said it would do and close with a new goal written down, which is what gives the next visit something to measure against.

steps.title: Nominate the chapters and members doing the work
steps.body: You see across a whole region, so you notice work that no single chapter would put forward for itself. Check the award's cycle first, because most close well before the award is presented.

steps.title: Nominate volunteers for national office
steps.body: You see more of the region's talent than anyone. Nominations are the pipeline for every national volunteer role.

role_guides.title: National Officer
role_guides.summary: National office opens the whole fraternity to you rather than one chapter. Every list you already know, such as events, forms, audits, ballots and scores, gains an all-chapters version, and the dashboards roll them up. This guide is the shared national surface. Which parts you live in depends on your seat: the Grand Treasurer works from balances and audits, the Grand Scribe from officer records and forms, the Grand Marshal from scores and tasks. If you also serve as a Regional Director, that guide covers what is specific to a region.

steps.title: Start at the national dashboard
steps.body: Chapter health across every region, covering scores, submissions and outstanding tasks, in one place. Every region has the same dashboard filtered to itself if you need to narrow it.

steps.title: Know who holds each office
steps.body: Officer records turn over every year, and writing to last year's Regent is the commonest way a message goes unread. The adviser list is your continuity when they do.

steps.title: Know who the advisers are
steps.body: Advisers stay in post while officers rotate, so they are usually the fastest way to get a straight answer about a chapter.

steps.title: Follow the scores
steps.body: Every chapter's score, side by side. This is the single number the fraternity uses to compare chapters, and it is built from everything else in this guide.

steps.title: Watch the money
steps.body: What every chapter owes the national office. If you hold the Grand Treasurer's seat this is your home page; for everyone else a growing balance is an early warning worth passing on.

steps.title: Clear the reviews waiting on you
steps.body: Events submitted for national review sit in a queue until an officer acts on them. Nothing chases you, so make a habit of opening it.

steps.title: See what chapters are running
steps.body: Every event across the fraternity, filterable by region and type, alongside the attendance dashboard that shows how many members actually turned up.

steps.title: Watch turnout, not just event counts
steps.body: The events and attendance dashboard pairs how much a chapter is running against how many members attend. The gap between the two is the number that matters.

steps.title: Read what chapters have filed
steps.body: Audits, bylaws, risk management signatures, health and safety programs and new member education programs each have an all-chapters view alongside the per-chapter one.

steps.title: Chase the chapters that are behind
steps.body: Outstanding chapter tasks are what the scores are built from. Every region has its own task list, so you can hand a region's overdue items straight to its Regional Director.

steps.title: Look a member up anywhere
steps.body: Search stops being limited to your own chapter once you hold national office.

steps.title: Leave notes for whoever holds your seat next
steps.body: Chapter and member notes are how the next officer knows what happened before they arrived.

steps.title: Set and review goals when you visit a chapter
steps.body: Goals are scoped to the chapter you are viewing as, so use the chapter switcher in the bar across the top of the page before you open them. A visit that starts from what the chapter set out to do, and ends with a new goal recorded, gives the next visit something to measure against.

steps.title: Nominate the chapters and members doing the work
steps.body: You see across the whole fraternity, so you notice work that no single chapter would put forward for itself. Check the award's cycle first, because most close well before the award is presented.

steps.title: Put the national officers on your phone
steps.body: The national officer directory has a Sync contacts button. Connect a Google or Microsoft account and the details stay current as seats change, or take a vCard file instead.

steps.title: Run a vote
steps.body: Ballots are created, distributed and counted here.
